title: Defensible point-in-time training panel: bounded Epoch–EvalPlus join audit

repository.canonical_changes: None. No repository edits, adapter, schema migration or model training.

scope.access: Public, unauthenticated, bounded exact-artifact and documentary reads only. No output archives, weights, training corpora, paid services or credentials.

decision.meaning: The three identified originals and selected aggregate measurements are auditable. None of the twelve candidates has the full executed-identity, run/protocol and information-set evidence required for a strict model-level training row. This does not establish that every other possible join is unusable.

artifact_counts.count_interpretation: 3626 source rows, 101 display labels, 202 versioned model objects and 808 metric slots are different populations. They are not independent model/run training examples. Selected12 give24 model objects and96 metric slots,76 numeric and20 null.

cutoff_and_information_sets.purpose: A deliberately explicit historical information cutoff for auditing feasible training features and outcome vintages; not a claim of an experiment run on that date.
cutoff_and_information_sets.epoch_current_vintage: The fresh CSV is byte-identical to the 2026 retained artifact. No pre-cutoff Epoch row/field vintage was verified. Last modified is not each field’s first availability.
cutoff_and_information_sets.reconstructable_features: Dated primary papers can separately establish pre-cutoff model sizes and compute inputs. A new 6ND calculation must retain its source inputs and present-day derivation rather than backdate the current Epoch estimate. The companion schema distinguishes source_value from reconstructed_from_pre_cutoff_inputs, keeps output public_availability separate from input_information_availability, and records derived_at. Inclusion based on historically available inputs is an explicit reconstruction policy, not a claim that the resulting number was published then.
forbidden_backdating: Current confidence labels without historical support
Revised compute estimates without a dated source
Current organization/accessibility/notability classifications without historical support
Late corrected benchmark values silently replacing an as-known-at-T target

A_repository_vintage.meaning: Conditional historical label availability if repository chronology is accepted. The Apr21 selected commit cannot establish first publication or an unseen future outcome.

B_repository_vintage.meaning: Selected B artifact is post-T. PR4 reuses earlier work; per-value first-public availability was not reconstructed. Do not infer every B value first appeared after T.

views.name: historical_training_at_T
views.rule: Use only features and training labels evidenced as available by T; a repository-chronology assumption must be explicit. Known historical labels are legitimate training data, not prospective holdouts.

views.name: corrected_hindsight
views.rule: Use explicitly selected later target vintages for retrospective science, without presenting them as knowledge at T; retain old assertions and supersession links.

views.name: prospective_prediction
views.rule: Require a defined prediction task and independently justified label/run timing. Neither a later repository commit nor a renamed product creates a future inference outcome.

cutoff_and_information_sets.canonical_clock_note: The canonical repository’s known_at refers to dataset ingestion, not historical publication. No evidence inspected in 2026 should receive a fabricated 2024 ingestion timestamp.

protocol_and_revision_findings.actual_metric_denominators: Unknown for individual runs. Suite-level counts are not substitutes for executed task manifests.

migration_text_counts.method: Static AST/text inspection, not executing the migration or downloading full task corpora.

protocol_and_revision_findings.change_interpretation: Published result revision with row-level inference/regrade mechanism unresolved. Keep issue, repair, affected run, regrade/rerun and publication events distinct.
protocol_and_revision_findings.human_eval_caveat: HumanEval and HumanEval+ values change too, despite unchanged declared HumanEval+ version. Do not assign all changes to MBPP task removal.
protocol_and_revision_findings.native_units: Reported percentage-valued greedy pass@1; preserve all four metric slots and source nulls. No inferred numerator, confidence interval, cross-benchmark average or p(doom).

intended_configuration.note: Available selector routing and defaults are not execution evidence. GPT-4-1106-preview has a JSON response-mode prompt path; prompted=true does not uniquely define a chat protocol.

missing_run_fields: Executed HF revision or requested/returned provider snapshot
protocol_and_revision_findings.presentation_fields: Ranks and cross-benchmark averages are HTML-derived, not native JSON measurements. B has60 MBPP nonnull labels versus78 inA; changed ranking populations and sequential tie handling cannot supply a longitudinal model outcome.

join_exclusion_table.identity_finding: A generic GPT-4 link and a May display label do not establish an invocation or served snapshot. March is a candidate generation; June is incompatible with a genuine May run, but the display month is not a measured inference timestamp.
join_exclusion_table.compute_and_cutoff_finding: Preserve 2.1e25 FLOP, Hardware, Likely and the notes-only 90% interval 8.2e24–4.4e25. Exact estimate vintage is unverified; the original developer report withheld compute and model size.

join_exclusion_table.identity_finding: The November 6 announcement supplies gpt-4-1106-preview as an available provider ID. A similarly named output asset is listed, but no row-to-run/output digest or served-model log connects it to the aggregate.
join_exclusion_table.compute_and_cutoff_finding: Numeric compute is blank. A 2.2e25 estimate occurs only in benchmark-imputed notes. Exclude that estimate from independent compute–performance analysis even if its historical date is later resolved.

join_exclusion_table.identity_finding: The April display label links the same November DevDay page. Current official documentation lists gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 and its changelog reports April 9 API general availability; neither identifies the executed model or independently preserves the historical page state.
join_exclusion_table.compute_and_cutoff_finding: Numeric compute is blank; notes contain 2.2e25 from benchmark imputation. Keep the source blank and exclude the imputed value.

join_exclusion_table.identity_finding: The snapshot links a generic release. The pre-cutoff code-llama-34b selector routes to Python-34B, while code-llama-multi-34b routes to base. Epoch notes explicitly calculate Python-34B. This supports intended variant consistency but not the actual selector or executed revision.
join_exclusion_table.compute_and_cutoff_finding: Preserve the approximate 5.3e23 total and 1.22e23 fine-tuning values. The numeric dataset-size cell is 600B while notes include 2.6T with ancestors; LCFT scope remains explicit. Epoch date August 14 differs from the August 24 release and paper.

join_exclusion_table.identity_finding: The snapshot explicitly links Python-70B. It is not the unqualified base model; both share upstream training stages.
join_exclusion_table.compute_and_cutoff_finding: Epoch 1.26e24 uses 2T ancestor plus 1T code tokens and omits Python specialization. Paper v3 prose says 1T for the 70B code stage, while its Figure 8 says 500B. Do not choose a stage count or manufacture a corrected total.

join_exclusion_table.identity_finding: The explicit Instruct handle differs from base and Python. The paper shows this 70B Instruct branch descending from Python; it is not the same tuning route as the smaller Instruct variants.
join_exclusion_table.compute_and_cutoff_finding: Do not copy the base 1.26e24 as Instruct total. Figure 8 adds 260M instruction tokens after a 100B Python branch, but the upstream 500B/1T conflict remains. Base LCFT is a sibling branch, not an automatic cost to add.

join_exclusion_table.identity_finding: Both sources name deepseek-ai/deepseek-coder-6.7b-base. Dated primary documentation confirms the size/base variant; execution revision and invocation configuration remain unknown.
join_exclusion_table.compute_and_cutoff_finding: 8.04e22 FLOP can be reconstructed now as 6 × 6.7e9 × 2e12 from pre-cutoff disclosed inputs. This is an estimate, not measured compute or proof the current Epoch cell existed then.

join_exclusion_table.identity_finding: The Epoch candidate is the base repository; EvalPlus names Instruct. The pinned card identifies the base initialization and an additional 2B instruction tokens.
join_exclusion_table.compute_and_cutoff_finding: The base 8.04e22 may be a separately named ancestral-pretraining predictor. It is not the descendant total, and the base/Instruct observations cannot be split independently.

join_exclusion_table.identity_finding: Both sources name deepseek-ai/deepseek-coder-33b-base. No executed revision or run time is recorded.
join_exclusion_table.compute_and_cutoff_finding: 3.96e23 FLOP is a current 6ND estimate reconstructable from the pre-cutoff 33B and 2T disclosures. B’s MBPP nulls stay missing, without forward-fill.

join_exclusion_table.identity_finding: The explicit bigcode/starcoder2-3b handle and pre-cutoff paper support the named 3B base variant. A documented repository state is not the executed state.
join_exclusion_table.compute_and_cutoff_finding: 5.94e22 FLOP appears in v1 Table 6, including base and long-context training. It is a developer-reported 6ND estimate, independent of benchmark-score imputation.

join_exclusion_table.identity_finding: The explicit 7B handle matches the named variant. A June 11 generation-configuration correction postdates T and cannot be assumed for an April execution.
join_exclusion_table.compute_and_cutoff_finding: 1.55e23 FLOP is the v1 Table 6 6ND estimate for base plus long-context training; missing MBPP B values do not become zeros.

join_exclusion_table.identity_finding: The explicit 15B base handle is consistent; keep it distinct from any Instruct/OCI variant. A June 5 generation-configuration update is documentary revision evidence, not a new training run.
join_exclusion_table.compute_and_cutoff_finding: 3.87e23 FLOP is the v1 Table 6 6ND estimate including base plus long-context training. Actual loaded checkpoint and protocol remain unresolved.

documentary_revision_anchors.warning: These pins identify documents/repository states inspected; none is asserted to be the state actually loaded by EvalPlus.

### 1. Introduction of Deepseek Coder Deepseek Coder is composed of a series of code language models, each trained from scratch on 2T tokens, with a composition of 87% code and 13% natural language in both English and Chinese. We provide various sizes of the code model, ranging from 1B to 33B versions. Each model is pre-trained on project-level code corpus by employing a window size of 16K and a extra fill-in-the-blank task, to support project-level code completion and infilling. For coding capabilities, Deepseek Coder achieves state-of-the-art performance among open-source code models on multiple programming languages and various benchmarks. - **Massive Training Data**: Trained from scratch on 2T tokens, including 87% code and 13% linguistic data in both English and Chinese languages. - **Highly Flexible & Scalable**: Offered in model sizes of 1.3B, 5.7B, 6.7B, and 33B, enabling users to choose the setup most suitable for their requirements. - **Superior Model Performance**: State-of-the-art performance among publicly available code models on HumanEval, MultiPL-E, MBPP, DS-1000, and APPS benchmarks. - **Advanced Code Completion Capabilities**: A window size of 16K and a fill-in-the-blank task, supporting project-level code completion and infilling tasks. ### 2. code_llama_compute_conflict.resolution: Unresolved within-version source conflict. Preserve both assertions and branch topology; do not repair the source, choose one value, or pool base/Python/Instruct total costs.

dependency_and_family_rules.rule: Deduplicate exact original blobs by SHA-256 and byte length; retain every version/URL/receipt. Reimporting an unchanged blob must not mint another scientific run.

Use checkpoint/service identity, generation/output set and evaluation specification for observation identity; artifact publication is a separate key. Unknown run IDs stay null and do not all collapse into one run.
Keep a model’s four metrics and both publication vintages in the same split group. Equal scores alone do not prove shared outputs; score changes alone do not prove a new run.

Union documented same-checkpoint, same-output, ancestor/descendant, quantization/conversion and distillation/teacher dependencies before splitting. Multi-parent derived models must not leak a known parent across folds.

Use four conservative family blocks for this bounded study: GPT-4, Code Llama, DeepSeek-Coder v1, StarCoder2. Family blocks are safeguards, not a claim that every member has identical weights or one independent pretraining run.

Represent a reused ancestor compute estimate once and link descendants. Base compute, post-training compute and total compute have different scopes. Do not count repeated ancestor estimates as independent evidence.
Record shared benchmark, evaluator, corpus, publication and estimate-source dependencies as additional clusters. A shared benchmark alone does not turn every model into one hard ancestry component.

A future adapter should use family-blocked and time-aware evaluation, fit preprocessing/feature selection only on the training side, report checkpoint and lineage counts, and conduct sensitivity analysis to uncertain ancestry. Four families are too few for a strong generalization estimate in this audit.

cases.name: Hosted alias and product do not identify an executed checkpoint
cases.fixture: EvalPlus GPT-4 (May 2023) links the GPT-4 research page; candidate Epoch rows describe March/June editions. The record supplies no invocation log identifying the requested and served model snapshot. April Turbo also requires ChatGPT versus API surface resolution.
cases.attempt: Match by GPT-4 plus date-like label and assign an exact API checkpoint or use a ChatGPT product announcement as proof of the evaluated API model.
cases.expected: Preserve the candidate and all dated assertions; record alias_only or ambiguous, executed checkpoint null, no strict executed-checkpoint inclusion. A publisher family or product link does not resolve run identity.
cases.must_not_do: Invent gpt-4-0314, gpt-4-0613, gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09, invocation dates or a universal product/API identity.

cases.name: Base, Python-specialized and instruction-tuned variants stay distinct
cases.fixture: The CodeLlama-70B result links CodeLlama-70b-Python-hf, while its display label omits Python. DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B-base and 6.7B-instruct are distinct EvalPlus keys, with a possible shared base-training lineage.
cases.attempt: Join by normalized family and parameter count; assign one score or total compute figure to both base and tuned variants.
cases.expected: Reject the proposed equivalence of unlike variants. Retain an explicitly evidenced ancestor link separately; ancestral pretraining compute may be a named predictor, while descendant total training compute stays missing. The same lineage group must not cross train/test folds.
cases.must_not_do: Infer base=tuned, Python=general base, or identical full training cost from names and parameter counts.

cases.name: Repository revision is not execution proof
cases.fixture: A StarCoder2 model card identifies a named repository and a dated revision; no EvalPlus record ties its run to that revision, full weight manifest, tokenizer and generation configuration. A later revision may alter only tokenizer or metadata.
cases.attempt: Use the latest Hub commit as the checkpoint executed in April 2024, or count a tokenizer/card correction as a newly trained model.
cases.expected: Store declared artifact identity separately from executed identity. Keep run revision null and exact-execution inclusion held. Distinguish weight, tokenizer/config and documentation revisions; retain the original dates and relationship evidence.
cases.must_not_do: Backdate a current commit, equate one shard digest with a complete loaded artifact set, or mint a new training example for metadata changes.

cases.name: Correction vintage is not a new inference run
cases.fixture: For CodeLlama-70B, HumanEval+ changes from 50.0 to 50.6; MBPP and MBPP+ change from 65.4/53.4 to null across A/B. Other rows have changed scores. The migration documents task removals and retained-prompt edits; run/output linkage remains unresolved.
cases.attempt: Interpret the April 21-to-22 difference as capability growth, as an independent second run, or solely as changing the MBPP denominator.
cases.expected: Keep both metric vintages and a published_revision_inference_unresolved relationship, with no fabricated run IDs. Preserve protocol/population changes and HumanEval+ changes too. Regrade_same_outputs requires documented output reuse; new_inference requires execution evidence.
cases.must_not_do: Normalize away the change, attribute all deltas to 399-to-378 membership, or increase unique-run/model counts.

cases.name: Explicit null, blank compute and uncertainty survive
cases.fixture: The same CodeLlama-70B B record has native MBPP/MBPP+ nulls. GPT-4 Turbo has blank numeric Training compute (FLOP) cells but compute notes containing an imputed value. Source confidence labels and numeric intervals have different meanings.
cases.attempt: Coerce missing scores or numeric blanks to zero, forward-fill A into B, silently parse a notes estimate as a native numeric cell, or convert a confidence label into a statistical interval.
cases.expected: Retain all eight metric slots per candidate; missing scores remain null with source-supported reasons. Preserve native compute blank and notes as separate evidence. Preserve reported intervals and labels without invented error bars. A notes extraction, if shown, is an explicitly derived field.
cases.must_not_do: Treat null as failure, assume unchanged old score, or relabel a qualitative confidence level as 95 percent uncertainty.

cases.name: Feature cutoff and label chronology are separate clocks
cases.fixture: T is 2024-04-20T23:59:59Z. A's bytes occur in ancestor ba37a9f43a5706e87762951029baab25880cd0d6 with repository timestamp 2024-04-20T03:06:04Z, although the selected A snapshot is dated April 21. Exact public-first-seen and inference times are not established. The inspected Epoch CSV has later Last modified dates and current citation counts; pre-T primary papers may support particular earlier values.
cases.attempt: Declare A an unseen future target because the selected commit is after T; backdate the current citation count or revised compute cell to model release; substitute B's later corrected score into the information known at T.
cases.expected: Keep first public and inference times unknown; label A repository_chronology_only and qualify any as-of training view by that assumption, with no prospective-outcome claim. Exclude current citation counts and unsupported revised cells from pre-T features. Admit a specific earlier value only with its pre-T source and derivation evidence. Preserve B as a separately dated corrected-hindsight view.
cases.must_not_do: Equate a Git timestamp with observed first public availability, reject genuinely historical labels from all training uses, or grant every field the row's model-release date.

cases.name: Benchmark-imputed compute cannot test independent compute versus performance
cases.fixture: Epoch's GPT-4 Turbo November and April rows contain blank numeric compute cells, notes stating an imputed 2.2e25 FLOP estimate and estimation method Benchmarks.
cases.attempt: Use that notes estimate as the independent compute predictor of EvalPlus performance, even if a source date before T were later established.
cases.expected: Preserve the raw blank, method and notes; mark the derived estimate benchmark_imputation and exclude it from the independent compute-performance view. Temporal availability alone cannot remove circularity. An independently evidenced replacement must be a new feature assertion with its own availability and scope.
cases.must_not_do: Treat the notes value as measured FLOP, assume an estimate is independent because a different benchmark produced it, or silently substitute it for missing native compute.

cases.name: Repeated publication and related models do not inflate independence
cases.fixture: A/B have identical sets of 101 model keys. This audit contains 12 candidates and 96 metric slots. Some assertions repeat unchanged, others revise prior measurements; multiple variants may share pretraining ancestors and compute estimates.
cases.attempt: Call the snapshots 202 independent examples, count every metric as an independent model, reimport identical artifacts as new runs, or randomly place related variants/measurement vintages into separate train/test folds.
cases.expected: Content-identical reimport adds provenance if needed but no duplicate observation/run. Keep raw-row, candidate, checkpoint, metric, output-set, pretraining-lineage and family counts separate. Group documented same-run/output and ancestor edges into indivisible connected components; conservatively group a family when ancestry is unresolved. Do not infer same run merely from equal scores.
cases.must_not_do: Count aliases, mirrors, revisions or reused ancestral compute as independent evidence; split a multi-parent derivative away from a known parent component.

proposed_acceptance_cases.execution_note: These are eight proposed acceptance cases. They were not implemented as an adapter or run as domain tests. Any JSON Schema parser/shape check is separate and does not establish these semantic properties.

smallest_missing_artifact.name: Publisher-authored EvalPlus aggregate-to-run manifest
smallest_missing_artifact.minimum_useful_scope: Start with the three StarCoder2 base labels and their HumanEval/HumanEval+ assertions across A/B, since pre-cutoff developer compute estimates are already available. Extend the same small manifest to the12 audited labels.
required_fields: Returned provider snapshot or loaded HF revision
A-to-B change relationship with reused-output versus new-inference evidence
First publication/availability evidence or an explicit unknown
smallest_missing_artifact.expected_benefit: Could upgrade multiple nominal joins without weights, corpus downloads or model execution. Five strong base-model feature candidates (three StarCoder2 and two DeepSeek-Coder) are closest; exact coverage gain depends on what the manifest establishes.
will_not_resolve: Unsupported historical Epoch citation or metadata vintages
smallest_missing_artifact.action_performed: Recommendation only. No maintainer contact or request was sent.

unique_new_documents.artifact_scope: Epoch AI models data download identified on the dataset page
unique_new_documents.conditions: Attribute Epoch AI and the source/authors; retain original/source attribution and identify any transformations.
unique_new_documents.publication_decision: License eligibility assessed; no public release authorized or performed.

unique_new_documents.conditions: Preserve license/attribution and change notices as applicable. Prior repository policy records no NOTICE file at these roots; that tree check was not repeated here.
